input_source: docs/daily_report/7.7/05_simple_head_term_seed_bank_2026-07-07.csv (328 rows, project's own Stage 1 inventory recommended candidate)
limitations: No historical baseline exists for these 328 exact queries (confirmed never-executed by docs/daily_report/7.11/.../TEST_DATA_INVENTORY_2026-07-11.md); regression assessment is behavior-based on current-state evidence, not historical before/after comparison.

Input dataset (05_simple_head_term_seed_bank) consists of bare single-word/short-phrase head terms, not natural multi-word user queries; this is a legitimate 'easy/common vocabulary' interpretation but is a harder case for a template-catalog matching system than richer natural-language queries would be -- this nuance is discussed in the report and should inform how the findings are weighted.

202/328 (61.6%) queries received direct human-equivalent relevance review (all zero-result, low-result, rewrite-triggered, >=1000, plus 30 random + 10 no-rewrite-normal controls, per Section 17's full-coverage-above-50% rule); the remaining 126 are no-rewrite queries with healthy (>=5, non-flooding) result counts not individually reviewed.

Mixed-language subset (contains_mixed_language) has only 2 members in this dataset (both false positives from single-character Latin substrings inside a CJK term, e.g. 'Z世代'), too small to draw a reliable mixed-language conclusion -- flagged rather than over-interpreted.

Wrong-entity and tokenizer-language-asymmetry findings (E046/E047 'Chris Wood' surname collision; zh/en festival-term asymmetry) are pattern observations from this run, not exhaustively re-verified against catalog content the way Prompt 7's Hard Query root-cause work was.
